artists.biography: Headswim (1992 - 2001)  One of the most sophisticated progressive rock bands to emerge from Britain in the last sixteen years. They are capable of dense, swilring epics and poignants heartbreakers. Probably at their best when they turn on the power.

perplexity.description:
Headswim's debut album Flood, originally released in 1994 on Epic Records, stands as a distinctive entry in the UK rock scene of the mid-1990s. Blending elements of psych-rock, grunge, and alternative, the album is characterized by its swirling guitar textures, dynamic rhythms, and introspective songwriting. Tracks like "Gone To Pot," "Soup," "Crawl," and "Dead" showcase the band's ability to merge heavy, distorted riffs with melodic sensibilities, creating a sound that was both atmospheric and accessible.

Flood marked Headswim's arrival as a promising new act, earning attention for its originality and energy within the crowded rock landscape of the era. Though the band did not achieve mainstream commercial success, the album was well-received by critics and developed a cult following over time. Its reputation as a "psych-grunge masterpiece" has endured, leading to later reissues and a deluxe edition by Trapped Animal in 2022, but its original 1994 release remains a significant milestone in Headswim's discography and a notable example of British alternative rock from the period.
